mechanism_narrative: The observed four-week upward trend in RETAIL_REC mobility, indicating a gradual return to pre-pandemic activity levels, will continue to drive further increases in retail and recreation visits over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: The mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is equal to or lower than the mean RETAIL_REC over the last 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decrease in RESIDENTIAL mobility below 10% from baseline, indicating a significant shift from staying at home to out-of-home activities, will trigger an increase in RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks as people seek more leisure options.
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL mobility remains below 10% for two consecutive weeks, but RETAIL_REC does not increase over the subsequent two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: The combined increase in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT mobility, signifying a return to office-based work and associated commuting, will lead to a rise in incidental retail and recreation visits during lunch breaks or after work, boosting RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both show week-on-week increases
failure_condition: Both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT mobility increase week-on-week for two consecutive weeks, but RETAIL_REC does not show an upward trend over the subsequent four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: As GROCERY_PHARM mobility approaches its baseline, indicating a normalization of essential errands, consumer confidence for non-essential activities will rise, leading to a positive shift in RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks, provided no new restrictions are imposed.
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM mobility remains within 2% of baseline for four weeks, but RETAIL_REC does not increase over the same period.

mechanism_narrative: The recent dip in PARKS mobility, following a previous rise, suggests a temporary shift in outdoor activity which will rebound quickly, diverting some leisure activity back to retail and recreation over the next week as people seek indoor alternatives or different outdoor venues.
candidate_trigger: PARKS mobility drops by more than 5 points week-on-week
failure_condition: PARKS mobility drops by more than 5 points week-on-week, but RETAIL_REC does not increase in the subsequent week.

mechanism_narrative: The broad upward trend observed across RETAIL_REC, GROCERY_PHARM, TRANSIT, and WORKPLACES indicates a widespread easing of restrictions and growing public confidence, which will collectively sustain and accelerate the recovery of RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: Despite consistent upward trends in at least three of the specified proxies, RETAIL_REC does not increase over the next four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: The inverse relationship between RESIDENTIAL and RETAIL_REC mobility, where decreasing time at home correlates with increasing out-of-home activities, suggests that the continued decline in RESIDENTIAL will directly drive further increases in RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL mobility decreases for two consecutive weeks, but RETAIL_REC does not increase over the subsequent two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained recovery in WORKPLACES mobility above -25% from baseline, indicating a critical mass of people returning to their jobs, will create a positive spillover effect on nearby retail and recreation establishments, boosting RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES mobility remains above -25% from baseline for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: WORKPLACES mobility remains above -25% for two consecutive weeks, but RETAIL_REC does not increase over the subsequent four weeks.
